reference.text: Disease cycle and epidemiology: The bacterium overwinters in infected seed, cotton stalks,
leaves, and unharvested bolls left standing or shallowly buried in the field (Sain et al., 2023).
The bacterium spreads through rain splash, irrigation water, and farm operations. When
infected seeds germinate, the bacteria wake up and attack the emerging plant, infect the
cotyledons, causing water-soaked, round lesions. This is the primary mode for introducing
the disease to new fields. Warm humid conditions favour disease development (Verma and
Singh, 1971). The pathogen enters the plant tissues through natural openings like stomata or
hydathodes, as well as through mechanical wounds caused by wind, hail, or cultivation tools.
Under warm, humid conditions, infected leaves exude a sticky, amber-colored bacterial ooze
packed with billions of active cells. Windy rain, overhead splash irrigation, and field
labourers brushing against wet plants carry this ooze from infected plants to healthy plants.
